rationale: Closed the non-owner boundary: the corrected-alias successor receipt measures the below-ballot case as violated (witness 12) and the above-ballot case as holding (index 17), so the recovery-authority account no longer carries a pending comparison. Both supporting behaviors now cite the corrected receipt, and the superseded alias-pinning defect is retained in the account with its cause.

knowledge.statement: In handlePrepareReply a reply whose Ballot differs from lb.lastTriedBallot increments lb.nacks and returns before the reply is appended to lb.prepareReplies, and the sub-case dispatch is guarded by len(lb.prepareReplies) >= SlowQuorumSize(); the only repair on the nack path (makeBallot plus a fresh bcastPrepare) is executed only while r.IsLeader is true. When every answering peer reports a stored ballot above the tried ballot, the appended count stays at the recovering replica's own self reply, so no sub-case is selected and no PreAccept, Accept or Commit is emitted for that attempt.
knowledge.conditions: Recovery where the replicas that answer the Prepare have a stored bal above the recovering replica's fixed tried ballot, so every answer is a rejection rather than a matching-ballot reply (epaxos/epaxos.go:1204-1235, with epaxos/epaxos.go:439-451 and 1216-1235).

knowledge.statement: makeBallot assigns the instance owner the ballot equal to its own replica id and any other recovering replica id+N, and advances it in steps of N only while r.IsLeader is true and the candidate is below maxRecvBallot; epaxos.New hardcodes IsLeader false and only the exported BeTheLeader RPC sets it, which the master invokes for the replica it designates. Repeating startRecoveryForInstance without that flag therefore reuses the identical ballot, whereas after the flag is set the same call emits a ballot above maxRecvBallot. For a non-owner, the boundary is the comparison between its fixed id+N ballot and the ballot the accepting peers have stored: id+N below that value is rejected inertly exactly as the owner's ballot is, while id+N above it is joined by the peers and the attempt advances.
knowledge.conditions: Any startRecoveryForInstance call in the captured snapshot, including repeat calls from executeCommands after COMMIT_GRACE_PERIOD (epaxos/epaxos.go:439-451, 1127-1150, 149-165, 1121-1125).

interpretations.rationale: Current account: recovery authority in the captured EPaxos package is bounded by the recovering replica's fixed ballot, and the boundary is measured with declared comparisons for both the instance owner and a non-owner. Owner case (receipt 911d45335b3047178a6fd739f24b2cfb, fixed experiment adfa9c6d31ca481896e5ca1277f6cdf4-experiment): two attempts at ballot 0 against peers storing 7 append only the self reply, dispatch nothing and emit no follow-up (comparisons 0 and 1 violated, witnesses 20 and 25), while the same call after the target's own BeTheLeader uses ballot 10, matches the peers and completes the instance (control comparisons 2 and 3 hold, evaluated 31 and 32). Non-owner boundary (receipt c342db60ffff4e42889bf53646049491, corrected successor of 43b9bbefd939404e9ad77b1e71564e2d-experiment, 23 parsed events, now without diagnostics): with the same premise of peers storing ballot 7, the attempt by replica 1 whose fixed ballot is 6 produces no matching reply, dispatches nothing and emits no follow-up (comparison 0 violated, witness 12), whereas the attempt by replica 3 whose fixed ballot is 8 is joined by the peers, matches two replies and dispatches its phase-1 proposal (comparison 1 holds, evaluated 17) - so the gate bites exactly when the recoverer's fixed ballot is below the stored one. The superseded boundary receipt c68b6de1442e45ffa00ddaf4df9b32e6 carries the same events; its comparisons came back violated/unknown only because both round-start prerequisite aliases had been left unpinned to their rounds, an observation-construction defect corrected in the successor. No repair exists inside the snapshot for the blocked case: makeBallot's climb and the nack path's recovery are both gated on IsLeader, so the blocked replica's attempts stay inert until the master designates it (epaxos/epaxos.go:439-451, 1216-1235, 1121-1125).
counterevidence: The gate is a boundary, not a blanket inability: the owner control and the above-ballot round both show the same instance advancing when the recoverer's ballot exceeds the stored one, so replicas whose fixed ballot is above the stored ballot are unaffected.
The peers' answers are legitimate protocol behaviour: each reports the ballot it stored, and the rejected tries were genuinely below it, so the rejections do not themselves violate a peer duty.

The blocked state requires a stored ballot above the recoverer's fixed ballot; in the receipts it came from a recovery attempt that failed after broadcasting its Prepare, which is a permitted failure but a specific one.

The recoverers that hold the instance without its command cannot substitute another path: their only entry point is startRecoveryForInstance, whose prepare uses makeBallot's fixed ballot; a replica that already holds the value is not blocked in the same way, as the value-adoption control showed.
limitations: One configuration (N=5, F=2, instance (0,0)) with the stored ballot fixed at 7; the boundary was exercised at fixed ballots 0, 6 and 8, so an intermediate stored ballot and higher ballot rounds (id+2N and beyond) were not exercised.

The harness invoked startRecoveryForInstance directly instead of waiting for the executor's COMMIT_GRACE_PERIOD retry (epaxos/epaxos.go:404-417) and scheduled all deliveries explicitly, so the retry cadence and transport timing are modelled.

The premise that the accepting peers store the higher ballot was produced by failing replica 2 after its Prepare broadcast; a real deployment could reach the same state through the same permitted failure, which was not exercised end-to-end.

No client or executor existed in these runs, so the blocked replica's consequence for a waiting client is characterised at the protocol level (an uncommitted instance whose dependents cannot execute) rather than measured as a completion interval.
interpretations.joint_history: Indices 0-6, 10, 11, 15-17, 20, 21, 23-28 and 31-35 belong to receipt 911d45335b3047178a6fd739f24b2cfb (owner-recoverer run); indices 8, 12, 14, 17, 19 and 20 belong to receipt c342db60ffff4e42889bf53646049491 (non-owner boundary run, same instance (0,0) and same scenario, corrected alias successor). Each statement names its receipt; no measurement is combined across executions.
